Image description: The diagram shows 11 hexagons arranged in three staggered rows. The top row has four hexagons: the leftmost contains 6, the next two are blank, and the rightmost contains a question mark. The middle row has three blank hexagons. The bottom row has four hexagons: the leftmost contains 4, the next two are blank, and the rightmost contains 11. Reasoning: Label the top row left-to-right as T1=6, T2, T3, T4=?, the middle row left-to-right as M1, M2, M3, and the bottom row left-to-right as B1=4, B2, B3, B4=11. Since all bold-point sums are equal, the six sums are T1+T2+M1, T2+T3+M2, T3+T4+M3, B1+B2+M1, B2+B3+M2, and B3+B4+M3. Compare the two sums sharing M1: T1+T2+M1 = B1+B2+M1, so 6+T2 = 4+B2, hence B2 = T2+2. Compare the two sums sharing M2: T2+T3+M2 = B2+B3+M2, so T2+T3 = B2+B3. Substituting B2=T2+2 gives T2+T3 = T2+2+B3, so B3 = T3-2. Compare the two sums sharing M3: T3+T4+M3 = B3+B4+M3, so T3+T4 = B3+11. Substituting B3=T3-2 gives T3+T4 = T3-2+11 = T3+9, so T4=9. Therefore the question-mark hexagon contains 9.
